item.title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
item.description: Introduced the transformer, the architecture behind essentially every modern language model.

item.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights (MIT CSAIL (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab))
item.description: The researchers' own account of eight experiments in which a frontier model (OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra) reads raw network weights to tell what a network does, writes game-playing and Go networks from scratch with no training, and removes a looping direction from Qwen3.5-0.8B by editing 0.016% of its weights, lifting MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. It is also candid about the limits: on a model that did not loop, the edits added nothing. Top of Hacker News and alphaXiv; a possible new route for both interpretability and optimisation.

item.title: Anthropic S-1 Breakdown (Kepler)
item.description: A line-by-line reading of the first financial statements ever published by a frontier AI lab, with every figure linked back to the filing: how compute is contracted 12-18 months ahead and expensed as capacity comes online, why an $80.7 billion half-year loss is mostly a non-cash accounting mark on convertible notes, and what roughly $600 billion in compute agreements and leased data centres mean for the company's cash. Makes the economics of a frontier lab concrete. Prepared from the public filing by a research firm that uses Claude in its product.
